title: Postural Hygiene, Joint Mobility, Flexibility and Foot Care
summary:
Pregnancy changes posture and body mechanics: the center of gravity moves forward, relaxin, estrogen and progesterone loosen ligaments, the base of support widens, and breast growth affects the shoulders and neck. These changes raise the risk of low back, sciatic and pelvic pain and fatigue. The chapter presents postural hygiene, joint mobility, flexibility and foot care as pillars for comfort and function.

It gives practical rules for standing, sitting, getting up and lifting, then mobility exercises for neck, spine, pelvis, hips and shoulders. Stretching guidance stresses gentle, controlled technique, and a foot-care section covers arch flattening, swelling and suitable footwear. Programs are individualized by activity level with supervision.
points: Postural education programs reduced lower back pain intensity by up to 45% in studies cited.
Wear comfortable shoes with a low heel (2-3 cm) and good cushioning.
When sitting, change position every 20-30 min, support the back and avoid crossing the legs.
Avoid lifting loads heavier than 10 kg (22 lbs); bend the knees, keep the back straight and hold the object close.
To get up, roll to the side, bend the knees and push up with the arms, avoiding sudden or twisting movements.
Mobility work is daily or 5-6 times a week, 10-20 min, at low intensity without pain, holding 5-10 s for 8-12 repetitions.
Static stretches are held 20-30 s per muscle with no bouncing or pain and with diaphragmatic breathing.
Targeted stretches cover hamstrings and glutes, pectorals, adductors and calves.
Feet may show flattened arches, swelling, altered gait, and on average 5 mm more length after a first pregnancy.
takeaways: Keep weight evenly on both feet and avoid standing for long periods.
Use a small lumbar pillow if needed when sitting.
Do a 10-20 min mobility routine as a morning warm-up or evening cool-down.
Do foot exercises: ankle circles, towel grasping, arch raises and plantar self-massage with a soft ball.
Choose shoes with flexible soles, stable heel counters and anatomical insoles; avoid high heels or unsupported flats.
Sedentary women can start with 15 min sessions of light mobility and breathing stretches.
cautions: Avoid forced stretches, bouncing and overstretching, because looser tissues raise injury risk.
Stop stretching if you experience dizziness, pain or muscle contractions.
Mobility exercises must be controlled because relaxin and progesterone reduce joint stability.
